# 15. Deployment Scenarios

Five scenarios exercise the full capability range of the protocol and serve as reference deployments for conformance validation.

## 15.1 Urban Signalized Intersection

An RSU mounted on a traffic signal transmits SPaT and MAP messages per SAE J2735 and acts as an O-CPS Class B participant: it transmits PerceptionSummary messages derived from roadside sensors (radar, camera) covering the intersection. Approaching vehicles fuse RSU perception with their own, anticipate cross-traffic behind occlusions, and trigger Intersection Assist advisories. Greenwave coordination (§13.2) is optional.

## 15.2 Limited-Access Highway Platoon

Three to six light passenger vehicles or commercial trucks form a C-ACC Group at highway speeds. The leader’s PerceptionSummary extends the effective forward sensor horizon of every follower by 100–400 meters. Fuel-efficiency gains for commercial platoons are a documented secondary benefit but are not claimed by this specification; the normative benefit is safety and anticipation.

## 15.3 Construction Zone

Temporary RSUs (portable or attached to trucks) broadcast construction-zone MAP deltas and high-confidence PerceptionSummary of workers on foot. Approaching vehicles widen gap targets automatically, and C-ACC Groups dissolve on zone entry if the group’s aggregate gap target would be shorter than the zone-posted minimum.

## 15.4 Vulnerable Road User (VRU) Proximity

A phone or dedicated beacon carried by a pedestrian or cyclist transmits a minimal PerceptionSummary containing its own pose and velocity, at low rate (1–2 Hz) and LOW-to-MEDIUM confidence. Vehicles fuse these into the world model as flagged vulnerable tracks, weighted appropriately. The pseudonymity and retention constraints of §11 apply unconditionally: no vehicle may retain or correlate VRU beacon data beyond 60 seconds.

## 15.5 Adversarial Conditions

A conformant deployment MUST remain safe under the presence of non-conforming or adversarial participants transmitting valid-signature messages with fabricated content. The mechanisms of §9.3 and §12.3 collectively reduce the impact of an adversary to, at worst, momentary spurious advisories before trust weights decay and misbehavior reports are filed. No adversary holding only a single compromised enrollment SHALL be able to induce unsafe actuation.
